title: Connect & Create Relay Scheme 2026: Professional Development and Mentoring for Young Communications Professionals in Africa
summary: Are you a journalist, communications professional, content creator, influencer, media presenter, or communications specialist based in Sub-Saharan Africa? The Connect Create Relay Scheme 2026 is offering an opportunity for young communications professionals to strengthen their skills, gain practical experience, and develop their professional networks while contributing to cultural projects in their own countries. The programme is part of Connect Create – Strengthening Cultural Ties Between Africa and Europe , an initiative focused on supporting cultural cooperation, professional development, mobility, networking, and sustainable connections between Sub-Saharan Africa and Europe. The Relay Scheme is specifically designed for early-career communications professionals with two to five years of professional experience in communications, journalism, media, or content creation. Selected participants will work directly with Creative Tandem projects in their respective countries while receiving structured professional development through training and individual mentoring. The programme will support 16 participants residing in 12 participating Sub-Saharan African countries and will run for approximately 11 months . What Is the Connect Create Relay Scheme? The Connect Create Relay Scheme is a professional development programme for young communications professionals working across the cultural and creative sectors. It forms part of the wider Connect Create programme, which is the Sub-Saharan Africa component of the Africa–Europe Partnerships for Culture programme. Connect Create is funded by the European Union and led by the Goethe-Institut and Expertise France , in partnership with the Institut français . The Relay Scheme itself is coordinated by Imago Médias . The wider Connect Create initiative aims to strengthen cultural relationships between Sub-Saharan Africa and the European Union through professional exchanges, capacity building, artistic cooperation, mobility, networking, and support for cultural professionals. The Relay Scheme focuses specifically on the communications side of this work. Participants will combine practical experience with structured learning, allowing them to contribute to cultural projects while strengthening their own professional capabilities. What Does the Relay Scheme Offer? The programme combines several forms of professional development. Participants will have the opportunity to: Work directly with a Creative Tandem project in their country. Gain practical experience in cultural communications. Participate in structured professional training. Receive individual mentoring. Develop their storytelling skills. Strengthen their social media communication skills. Improve editorial planning and strategy. Gain experience in press and media relations. Develop their cultural reporting capabilities. Build connections with communications professionals from other participating African countries. Become part of the wider Connect Create professional ecosystem. Receive a training certificate. Receive an allowance for communication activities carried out for the supported project. The official programme description confirms that participants will complete 10 themed training sessions covering areas such as storytelling, social media, editorial strategy, and press relations, alongside one-to-one mentoring. Who Is the Programme Designed For? The Connect Create Relay Scheme is aimed at young communications professionals who already have professional experience but are still developing their careers. Eligible professional profiles include: Journalists Communications professionals Communications specialists Content creators Influencers Media hosts Media presenters Applicants should have between two and five years of professional experience in communications, journalism, media, or content creation. The programme is particularly relevant to professionals who have already built some experience and an audience but want to strengthen their professional skills through practical cultural communications work. Age Requirement Applicants must be over 18 years old . This means applicants must have reached adulthood by the time of application. The programme is intended for young professionals, but the official eligibility requirement specifically establishes that applicants must be over 18 rather than giving a separate upper age limit. Professional Experience Requirement Applicants must have two to five years of professional experience in one or more of the following areas: Communications Journalism Media Content creation This requirement means the programme is not intended solely for people who are completely new to communications. Applicants should be able to demonstrate previous professional work and provide evidence through their CV and portfolio. Interest in Culture and the Creative Industries Applicants should have an interest in: Performing arts Music Cultural communication Cultural reporting Creative industries Arts and culture-related projects The programme connects communications professionals with Creative Tandem projects, meaning applicants should be interested in communicating cultural and creative work to audiences. This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to professionals who enjoy storytelling, cultural journalism, digital media, social media, arts communication, and creative-sector content. Audience and Local Presence Applicants should have an active audience and demonstrate a meaningful local presence. This can be demonstrated through: Social media platforms Media platforms Community networks Professional networks Other relevant communication channels The official programme states that particular attention will be paid to applicants experience, motivation, local roots, and audience reach . This means applicants should not only demonstrate professional experience but should also show that they understand and engage with their local communities and audiences. Language Requirement Applicants must be proficient in either: English , or French Applications can be submitted in either English or French. The CV and portfolio materials should therefore be prepared in one of the accepted languages where required. Eligible Countries The Connect Create Relay Scheme is open to applicants residing in one of 12 participating countries . These countries are: South Africa Benin Cameroon Ghana Guinea Kenya Mali Mozambique Uganda Republic of the Congo Rwanda Senegal Applicants must reside in one of these countries to be eligible for the Relay Scheme. Applicants living in other African countries should not assume that they are eligible simply because the programme is generally focused on Sub-Saharan Africa. The Relay Scheme specifically identifies these 12 participating countries. What Will Participants Do? Participants will work directly with a Creative Tandem project in their own country . The practical component allows participants to apply their communications skills to real cultural projects rather than learning only through theoretical training. Depending on the project and participant s role, activities may involve areas such as: Storytelling Participants can use storytelling techniques to communicate the ideas, people, activities, and impact associated with cultural projects. Effective storytelling can help audiences understand why a cultural project matters and encourage greater engagement. Social Media Participants will develop experience communicating cultural projects through social media. This can include developing content, engaging audiences, supporting campaigns, and using appropriate platforms to increase visibility. Editorial Planning Editorial strategy is another important component of the programme. Participants can develop skills in planning content, identifying relevant themes, structuring communications activities, and maintaining consistent messaging. Media Relations Participants can gain practical exposure to communicating with media outlets and journalists. This can include developing media-facing content and supporting efforts to generate media attention for cultural projects. Cultural Reporting The programme also provides an opportunity to develop experience in cultural reporting and communications. This can involve communicating stories related to performing arts, music, cultural activities, creative practitioners, and related projects. Training Programme The professional development component includes 10 themed training sessions . The official programme identifies areas including: Storytelling Social media Editorial strategy Press relations The sessions are designed to strengthen participants practical communications capabilities while they work on their assigned cultural projects. The training component allows participants to complement their existing professional experience with structured learning. Individual Mentoring Participants will also receive one-to-one mentoring . Individual mentoring can provide a more personalized professional development experience, allowing participants to receive guidance relevant to their own career development and communications work. Combined with the group training sessions and practical project experience, the mentoring component creates a multi-dimensional professional development structure. Professional Network Another important benefit of the programme is access to a professional network. Participants will have opportunities to connect with communications professionals from the participating African countries as well as the broader Connect Create ecosystem. This can help participants: Exchange ideas. Learn from professionals in other countries. Discover different approaches to cultural communications. Build professional relationships. Explore potential future collaborations. Gain exposure to regional cultural and creative networks. For early-career communications professionals, these connections can become an important part of long-term professional development. Training Certificate Participants will receive a training certificate as part of the programme. A certificate can provide formal documentation of participation in the professional development programme and can be included in future professional portfolios, CVs, and applications where appropriate. Financial Support The programme provides an allowance for communication activities carried out for the supported project . The information provided does not specify a single fixed amount for the allowance. Applicants should therefore consult the official guidelines for the precise financial arrangements, eligible activities, and any applicable conditions. Programme Duration The Relay Scheme provides approximately 11 months of support . According to the official timeline, the programme is expected to begin in late January or early February 2027 . This extended period allows participants to combine practical project work with training, mentoring, and professional networking. Application Timeline Applicants should pay close attention to the programme timeline. Applications Open 15 September 2026 Application Deadline 13 October 2026 Shortlisting 14 October to 3 November 2026 During this period, applications will be reviewed and candidates will be shortlisted. Creative Tandem Project Proposal 5 to 19 November 2026 Shortlisted candidates will be asked to submit a proposal for a Creative Tandem project. Announcement of the 16 Connect Create Hubs 7 December 2026 The selected hubs will be announced. Programme Start Late January or early February 2027 The professional development programme is expected to begin around this period. Application Requirements Applicants are required to submit an online application. The application should include: 1. Online Application Form Applicants must complete the designated online application form. 2. Short CV Applicants must provide a short CV in either English or French . The CV should clearly demonstrate relevant professional experience in communications, journalism, media, or content creation. 3. Portfolio Applicants must provide a portfolio containing two to three examples of previous work . The portfolio is important because it allows applicants to demonstrate their practical communications capabilities rather than relying solely on descriptions in their CV. Examples could include relevant work such as: Published articles Journalism work Social media campaigns Digital content Cultural reporting Video or multimedia content Editorial projects Communications campaigns Media work Other professional communications outputs Applicants should choose examples that best demonstrate their communication skills and experience. How to Prepare a Strong Application Applicants should approach the application as an opportunity to demonstrate both professional experience and a clear interest in cultural communications. Demonstrate Relevant Experience Clearly explain your professional experience over the last two to five years. Focus on work that demonstrates communications, journalism, media, content creation, storytelling, or audience engagement. Make Your Portfolio Relevant Do not simply submit random examples of previous work. Choose two or three pieces that demonstrate your strongest and most relevant communications abilities. Where possible, select work that demonstrates: Storytelling Audience engagement Editorial judgment Social media communication Cultural or community reporting Media relations Creative content production Demonstrate Local Understanding Because the programme emphasizes local roots and working with Creative Tandem projects in participants countries, applicants should demonstrate their understanding of their local audience and cultural environment. Explain Your Motivation Applicants should clearly communicate why they are interested in cultural communications and how participation in the programme could contribute to their professional development. Highlight Audience Reach If you have an established audience through social media, media platforms, websites, community networks, or other channels, provide relevant evidence. Audience reach should be presented accurately and, where possible, supported with measurable information. Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity may be particularly relevant to professionals who want to combine communications with culture and the creative industries. Potential applicants include: Early-career journalists Digital communications professionals Social media professionals Content creators Cultural journalists Media presenters Influencers Storytellers Communications specialists Creative-sector communicators The strongest fit will generally be professionals who can demonstrate relevant experience, an active audience, local connections, and a genuine interest in performing arts, music, and cultural industries. About Connect Create The Relay Scheme forms part of the broader Connect Create – Strengthening Cultural Ties Between Africa and Europe programme. Connect Create is the Sub-Saharan Africa component of the Africa–Europe Partnerships for Culture programme, which is funded by the European Union. The wider initiative aims to strengthen cultural ties between Sub-Saharan Africa and the European Union through cooperation, inclusion, sustainability, professional development, and cultural exchange. The programme includes several support areas for professionals in performing arts and music, including: Connect Create Relay Scheme Mentoring Scheme Circulation of Performing Arts and Music Professional Mobility Creative Tandems The Relay Scheme specifically focuses on communications professionals. Focus on Young Professionals Connect Create places particular emphasis on younger generations and emerging cultural scenes. The wider programme recognizes the importance of young people s creativity, energy, and leadership in shaping future Africa–Europe cultural relationships. The programme also highlights priorities including: Supporting younger generations Promoting emerging cultural scenes Originality Connection to local context Sustainable collaboration Environmentally responsible approaches Inclusion Accessibility Key Details at a Glance Detail Information Programme Connect Create Relay Scheme Focus Cultural communications and professional development Number of participants 16 Programme duration 11 months Target professionals Journalists, communications specialists, content creators, influencers, media presenters Experience 2–5 years Age Over 18 Language English or French Geographic eligibility 12 specified Sub-Saharan African countries Training 10 themed sessions Mentoring One-to-one mentoring Practical experience Work with a Creative Tandem project Certificate Training certificate Support Allowance for communication activities Application opening 15 September 2026 Application deadline 13 October 2026 Shortlisting 14 October–3 November 2026 Proposal stage 5–19 November 2026 Selected hubs announced 7 December 2026 Programme start Late January/early February 2027 Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the Connect Create Relay Scheme 2026 is: 13 October 2026 Applications must be submitted through the official online application process. Applicants should not wait until the final day to prepare their CV and portfolio, particularly because the portfolio is an important part of the application. The official Institut français page confirms the application opening date of 15 September 2026 and the deadline of 13 October 2026. Click HERE to read more and apply. Conclusion The Connect Create Relay Scheme 2026 offers young communications professionals in selected Sub-Saharan African countries an opportunity to combine practical cultural communications work with structured professional development. Through an approximately 11-month programme, selected participants will work with Creative Tandem projects in their countries while receiving training in areas such as storytelling, social media, editorial strategy, and press relations. They will also receive individual mentoring, a training certificate, professional networking opportunities, and an allowance for communication activities associated with their supported project. The opportunity is particularly relevant to journalists, communications professionals, content creators, influencers, and media presenters who already have two to five years of professional experience and have developed an active audience or meaningful local presence. Applications are open from 15 September 2026 until 13 October 2026 . Eligible professionals who are interested in cultural communications, performing arts, music, and the creative industries should review the official guidelines, prepare a strong CV and portfolio, and submit their application before the deadline. title: InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ Turn Your Green Idea Into a Viable, Market-Ready Solution
summary: Do you have an innovative idea that could help businesses, communities, or cities become more sustainable, resource-efficient, and environmentally responsible? The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is designed to help promising green and circular-economy ideas move from early concepts to practical, viable, and market-ready solutions. The program supports university students, young innovators, researchers, startups, entrepreneurs, and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in the West Bank, including Jerusalem , who are working on solutions related to the green and circular economy. Through a combination of hackathons, specialized mentoring, technical assistance, incubation, networking, and seed funding , participants can receive practical support to develop, test, refine, and implement their ideas. The program provides financial support averaging approximately €8,000 per selected team , together with technical assistance, mentoring, guidance, and incubation support for up to six months. Applications for the InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program are scheduled to open in September 2026 . What Is InnoTadweer: EcoHack+? InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ is an innovation and entrepreneurship support program focused on developing solutions that contribute to a greener and more circular economy in the West Bank. The program is intended for people and organizations with ideas, prototypes, businesses, or existing facilities that could benefit from adopting more sustainable practices. Rather than focusing only on generating ideas, EcoHack+ aims to help participants move through the development process toward practical implementation and market readiness. The program combines several forms of support, including: Hackathons Technical assistance Specialized mentoring Expert guidance Incubation Networking Multidisciplinary team formation Seed funding Support for testing and refining solutions Assistance in moving ideas toward implementation and market readiness This combination allows participants to address both the technical and business aspects of green innovation. The Green and Circular Economy Focus The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program focuses on innovations that can improve the way resources are produced, consumed, reused, recovered, and managed. The green and circular economy approach seeks to reduce waste and resource consumption while creating sustainable economic opportunities. The program welcomes ideas and solutions related to areas such as: Resource Efficiency Solutions that help businesses, organizations, communities, or other users make more efficient use of resources can be considered. This may include innovations that reduce unnecessary consumption of materials, water, energy, or other resources. Waste Valorization EcoHack+ is interested in approaches that transform waste into economic value. Instead of treating waste solely as something to dispose of, participants can explore ways to recover, reuse, process, or convert waste into useful materials, products, or other forms of value. Circular Business Models Participants can develop business models based on circular economy principles. These may involve approaches that extend product lifecycles, encourage reuse, improve recycling, recover valuable materials, reduce waste, or create alternative approaches to resource consumption. Renewable Energy The program also welcomes innovative solutions related to renewable energy and the transition toward more sustainable energy systems. Sustainable Production Ideas that help businesses produce goods or services more sustainably can also fit within the program s focus. This can include approaches designed to reduce resource use, minimize waste, improve production efficiency, or incorporate environmentally responsible processes. Green Technologies EcoHack+ welcomes technological solutions that address environmental and sustainability challenges. Green technologies can potentially be applied across different industries and sectors, depending on the specific challenge being addressed. Sustainable Agriculture The program also includes solutions related to sustainable agriculture and resource-efficient agricultural practices. Participants can explore innovative approaches that contribute to more sustainable agricultural production and resource management. Other Green and Circular Economy Challenges The program is not limited to the examples listed above. It also welcomes other innovative approaches addressing challenges connected to the green and circular economy. Who Can Participate? InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ is designed for a broad range of innovators and organizations. Potential participants include: University students Young innovators Researchers Entrepreneurs Early-stage startups Informal teams Existing micro enterprises Small enterprises Medium enterprises The program therefore accommodates participants at different stages of development, from individuals who have only an initial idea to businesses and organizations that already have an operating facility and want to introduce more sustainable practices. Individual and Team Applications Participants do not necessarily need to have an established team before applying. Applications can be submitted: Individually As part of an existing team For participants who apply individually, the program provides opportunities to connect with people from different disciplines, professional backgrounds, and areas of expertise. This is particularly important because many environmental and circular-economy challenges require collaboration between people with different technical, business, scientific, entrepreneurial, and practical skills. During the hackathon component, participants can receive support in developing multidisciplinary teams. Track A: Idea Development One of the program s tracks is Track A – Idea Development . This track is intended for participants who have an idea but may not yet know how to develop it into a practical solution. It is particularly relevant to: University students Young innovators Entrepreneurs Informal teams Individuals with early-stage ideas The track focuses on early-stage idea development, particularly in the areas of: Resource efficiency Sustainable production Green innovation Circular economy solutions Participants in this stage can use the program s support to develop their initial concept and begin determining how it could become a viable solution. From Idea to Market-Ready Solution A major objective of EcoHack+ is to help participants progress through the different stages of innovation. An idea may initially exist only as a concept. Through the program, participants can receive support to develop and refine that concept. The development process can involve: 1. Identifying the Problem Participants begin by understanding the environmental, resource-efficiency, or circular-economy problem they are attempting to solve. A clearly defined problem can provide the foundation for developing a practical solution. 2. Developing the Idea Participants can work on transforming an initial idea into a more clearly defined innovation or project. This may involve identifying the target users, defining the proposed solution, and determining how the solution could address the identified challenge. 3. Building or Refining a Prototype For participants who already have a prototype, the program can provide support to further develop and refine it. The objective is to move beyond an initial concept toward something that can be tested and evaluated. 4. Mentoring and Technical Assistance Participants receive access to technical assistance, specialized mentoring, and guidance. Expert support can help participants identify challenges, improve their solutions, and consider technical and business requirements. 5. Incubation Selected participants can receive incubation support for up to six months . This provides additional time and support for developing the idea, project, or business. 6. Financial Support Selected teams can receive financial support averaging approximately €8,000 . The funding can provide resources needed to advance a promising solution toward implementation and market readiness, subject to the program s funding requirements and selection procedures. Expected Benefits of the Program Participants selected for InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ can benefit from several forms of support. Financial Support Selected teams are expected to receive financial support averaging around €8,000 . The funding component can help selected teams move their ideas forward and support the development of green or circular-economy solutions. Technical Assistance Participants can receive dedicated technical assistance relevant to developing and improving their solutions. Specialized Mentoring Expert mentors can provide guidance as participants develop their ideas, prototypes, projects, or businesses. Incubation Support Selected participants can receive incubation support for up to six months. Networking Opportunities Participants can connect with people from different professional and academic backgrounds. This can help individuals find collaborators and build multidisciplinary teams. Market Readiness The program aims to help promising ideas progress toward implementation and market readiness. This is particularly important for participants who want to transform an environmental concept into a practical product, service, business model, or project. Who Might Benefit From Applying? The program can be relevant to individuals and organizations at different stages. For example, a university student with an early idea related to waste management could use the program to develop the concept further. A young entrepreneur could use the program to refine a circular business model. A researcher could explore how research findings can be translated into a practical green innovation. An early-stage startup could receive mentoring and funding to improve an existing prototype. An existing MSME could explore how to introduce more resource-efficient or sustainable practices into its operations. The program s broad structure allows different types of applicants to approach green innovation from different starting points. Program Duration The stated duration of the InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is: 18 months Within this broader program period, participants can engage with different activities and forms of support depending on their track and stage of development. Application Period The application period is scheduled to open in: September 2026 The information provided does not specify a final application deadline. Applicants should therefore monitor the official InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ application information for the opening announcement, submission deadline, application requirements, and any updates to the program schedule. Program Geographic Focus The program is implemented in the West Bank, including Jerusalem . Its focus is therefore on supporting green innovation, entrepreneurship, resource efficiency, and circular-economy development within the Palestinian context. Applicants should review the official program eligibility requirements before applying to confirm their geographic eligibility. Supporting Organizations The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program is implemented within the Green West Bank and SAWA 2 projects. The program is supported by: The European Union The Belgian Government through DGD Implementation is led by the Belgian Agency for International Cooperation (ENAPEL) in partnership with the Business Center for Innovation, Technology and Entrepreneurship (BCite) at Al-Quds University . The collaboration brings together international development support and local innovation and entrepreneurship expertise. Contribution to the Palestinian Green Economy The program is part of broader efforts to support a greener and more circular Palestinian economy. Through support for green innovation and entrepreneurship, the program seeks to contribute to: Green innovation Entrepreneurship Business competitiveness Resource efficiency Sustainable production Circular economy development Environmental solutions Market-oriented innovation Supporting innovative businesses and young people can also contribute to the development of new products, services, business models, and technologies addressing environmental challenges. Why Multidisciplinary Collaboration Matters Many sustainability challenges cannot be solved through one area of expertise alone. For example, developing a solution for waste valorization may require technical knowledge, environmental expertise, business planning, market research, finance, design, and communication. Similarly, a renewable-energy innovation may require engineering expertise alongside entrepreneurship and business-development skills. EcoHack+ therefore encourages participants from different backgrounds to collaborate. Applicants who do not yet have a team can potentially use the hackathon and networking activities to meet other participants and form multidisciplinary teams. What Applicants Should Consider Before Applying Potential applicants should consider several questions before submitting an application. Clearly Define the Problem What environmental or resource-efficiency challenge does your idea address? Explain the Proposed Solution How does your idea address the problem? Identify the Target Users Who would use or benefit from the solution? Consider Sustainability How would the solution contribute to a greener or more circular economy? Think About Feasibility Can the idea realistically be developed, tested, implemented, or scaled? Consider the Market If the solution is commercial, who would pay for it and why? Identify the Stage of Development Is your idea: An early concept? A prototype? An existing startup? An established MSME looking to adopt sustainable practices? Understanding the current stage of the project can help applicants determine which program track is most appropriate. Click HERE to read more and apply. Conclusion The InnoTadweer: EcoHack+ program provides a structured pathway for developing innovative solutions to environmental and resource-efficiency challenges in the West Bank, including Jerusalem. By combining hackathons, technical assistance, specialized mentoring, networking, incubation, and seed funding, the program is designed to help participants move from an initial idea or existing project toward a more developed and potentially market-ready solution. The program is open to different types of innovators, including university students, young innovators, researchers, early-stage startups, entrepreneurs, and micro, small and medium enterprises. Participants can apply individually or as teams, with opportunities to form multidisciplinary teams during the hackathon. With average financial support of approximately €8,000 per selected team and incubation support of up to six months, EcoHack+ provides both financial and non-financial assistance to participants working on green and circular-economy solutions. The application period is scheduled to open in September 2026 . Since a specific closing date was not provided in the information available, interested applicants should monitor the official program announcement and application platform for the deadline and complete eligibility requirements. title: Goldman Sachs 2026 Emerging Leaders Series: Explore Future Summer Analyst Opportunities
summary: The Goldman Sachs 2026 Emerging Leaders Series is an exploratory career development program designed to introduce promising undergraduate and master s students to future opportunities at one of the world s leading financial services firms. The program provides participants with an opportunity to explore different business areas at Goldman Sachs, develop professional and recruiting skills, interact with employees and senior leaders, and gain insight into the firm s Summer Analyst opportunities. Through business-specific training, interview preparation, networking activities, group exercises, and engagement with professionals, participants can gain a better understanding of the skills required to pursue future internship opportunities at Goldman Sachs. Applications for the 2026 Emerging Leaders Series are currently open, with the application deadline set for Sunday, October 4, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time (ET) . About the Goldman Sachs Emerging Leaders Series The Emerging Leaders Series is an exploratory program intended to help students prepare for future recruiting opportunities at Goldman Sachs. Rather than being a traditional internship, the program is designed to provide participants with early exposure to Goldman Sachs businesses and recruiting process. Participants will have opportunities to: Learn more about Goldman Sachs and its different business divisions. Explore potential career paths within the firm. Participate in business-specific training. Develop professional and career-related skills. Take part in interview preparation activities. Participate in group activities. Network with Goldman Sachs professionals. Engage with senior leaders. Learn more about future Summer Analyst opportunities. Gain insights into the recruiting process. Explore a specific Goldman Sachs business track. Potentially visit one of Goldman Sachs offices in New York, Dallas, or Salt Lake City, depending on the business track. Networking Networking is another central component of the program. Participants will have opportunities to interact with Goldman Sachs professionals and potentially senior leaders. Group Activities Participants will also take part in group activities designed to encourage collaboration, communication, and engagement with other emerging professionals. title: Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program: Applications Open for $100,000–$250,000 Grants to Support Small Businesses
summary: The Visa Foundation has launched the U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program , a new grant opportunity designed to strengthen nonprofit organizations that provide direct support to small and micro businesses across the United States. Through the program, Visa Foundation is committing $2 million in grant funding to nonprofit Entrepreneurial Support Organizations (ESOs). Selected organizations will receive flexible, 12-month grants ranging from $100,000 to $250,000 to strengthen their capacity, expand their services, and help small and micro businesses become more resilient, competitive, and positioned for sustainable growth. Applications are open and must be submitted by October 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM (noon) Pacific Time . The program is administered by Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors (RPA) , which is responsible for managing the Request for Proposals process and grantmaking activities. Overview of the Visa Foundation Grant Program Small and micro businesses play an important role in creating employment, generating income, supporting local communities, and contributing to economic development. However, many small businesses face challenges in accessing the knowledge, technical assistance, technology, training, and other resources required to grow and remain competitive. The Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program seeks to address some of these challenges indirectly by investing in organizations that already work closely with small and micro businesses. Rather than providing grants directly to individual entrepreneurs, the program provides funding to nonprofit Entrepreneurial Support Organizations that deliver services to operating small and micro businesses. The goal is therefore to strengthen the organizations that make up the small-business support ecosystem and enable them to reach more businesses, improve their services, and increase their impact. According to the program information, Visa Foundation is committing $2 million to the initiative, while RPA is administering the application and grantmaking process. What Funding Is Available? Successful applicants are expected to receive grants ranging from: $100,000 to $250,000 12-month grant period Grants beginning in January 2027 Flexible funding that can support both programming and organizational operations The exact grant amount will be determined in relation to the size of the applicant organization. This flexibility is an important feature of the opportunity because organizations can use the funding to strengthen both the services they provide and the internal capacity required to deliver those services effectively. What Can the Grant Funding Be Used For? The program allows grant funding to support a broad range of activities connected to strengthening an organization s ability to serve small and micro businesses. Eligible uses may include: 1. Business Training Organizations can use funding to strengthen or expand training programs that provide entrepreneurs and business owners with practical knowledge and skills. Training may form part of an organization s existing programming or be introduced or expanded through the grant. 2. Technical Assistance Funding can support technical assistance designed to help small and micro businesses overcome specific operational or business-development challenges. 3. Business Coaching Organizations may use grant resources to expand coaching and support services that help operating businesses make informed decisions and improve their resilience and growth prospects. 4. Digital Adoption and Technology The program recognizes the growing importance of technology and digital tools for small businesses. Funding may therefore support services that help businesses adopt technology, use digital tools, and respond to changing market conditions. The program specifically identifies helping small and micro businesses navigate AI, digital tools, and technology adoption as an area that may receive priority consideration. 5. Staffing Grant resources can also contribute to organizational staffing needs where this strengthens the applicant s capacity to provide direct services to small and micro businesses. 6. Administrative and Operational Costs The funding is flexible enough to support certain operational needs, including administrative costs, where those expenses contribute to the organization s ability to deliver and expand its work. Applicants will need to explain how the requested funding would strengthen their organization and increase its impact on the small-business community. Who Is Eligible to Apply? The opportunity is intended for nonprofit Entrepreneurial Support Organizations (ESOs) that directly support operating small and micro businesses. To qualify, an organization must meet the program s eligibility requirements. U.S. 501(c)(3) Status Applicants must be U.S.-based public charities with valid 501(c)(3) status and must comply with applicable 501(c)(3) requirements. Organizational Budget Applicants must have an annual operating budget between: $1 million and $10 million. This requirement means the program is aimed at established, mid-sized to large organizations rather than very early-stage nonprofit organizations. Direct Services to Small and Micro Businesses Organizations must directly provide business-support services to operating small and micro businesses. Examples of qualifying services include: Business training Coaching Technical assistance Peer learning Technology adoption support The purpose of these services should be to help small and micro businesses strengthen their growth, resilience, and competitiveness. Financial Documentation Applicants must have two years of audited financial statements and/or IRS Form 990s. Applicants will also need to provide their current board-approved operating budget showing anticipated revenues and expenses for 2026 and 2027 . Can Fiscally Sponsored Organizations Apply? Yes. Fiscally sponsored organizations can apply if their fiscal sponsor has valid 501(c)(3) status and the fiscally sponsored organization meets all other eligibility requirements. Additional documentation may be required, including: Fiscal sponsor governance materials List of directors and their affiliations Two years of audited financials IRS Form 990 Signed fiscal sponsorship agreement or memorandum of understanding Therefore, being fiscally sponsored does not automatically exclude an organization from consideration. Can Local Chapters of National Organizations Apply? Yes, local chapters may be considered if they have standalone 501(c)(3) status and meet the remaining eligibility requirements. Organizations should therefore carefully verify their legal and financial structure before beginning an application. Can Previous Visa Foundation Grantees Apply? Yes. Past and current grantees of Visa Foundation or Visa Inc. are eligible to apply, provided they meet the other requirements of the program. What Types of Small Businesses Does the Program Support? The program defines small and micro businesses as independently owned businesses that are currently operating and actively selling products or services. While there are no strict numerical cutoffs, the program states that qualifying businesses would generally have: 50 or fewer employees $1.5 million or less in annual revenue The focus is therefore on operating businesses rather than individuals who are only considering starting a business. What Organizations May Be Particularly Competitive? Although all eligible applications will be reviewed, the program identifies several characteristics that may strengthen an organization s application. Organizations are encouraged to demonstrate: A strong understanding of small and micro business challenges and opportunities Trusted relationships with the communities they serve The ability to adapt to changing market needs Experience helping businesses use AI, digital tools, and technology Meaningful and measurable impact on business growth and resilience A commitment to continuous learning and collaboration The organizational capacity to strengthen or expand services using grant funding These priorities indicate that applicants should be able to demonstrate not only what they do, but also the measurable difference their services make for the businesses they support. Which Organizations May Be Less Competitive? The program states that eligible organizations may be less competitive if they: Are not primarily focused on providing direct business-support services to small and micro businesses. Primarily support aspiring entrepreneurs or idea-stage businesses rather than currently operating businesses. Reach fewer than 200 small and micro businesses per year . Cannot demonstrate outcomes or evidence of impact. Propose grant uses that are not clearly connected to strengthening small-business growth and resilience. Meeting the basic eligibility requirements therefore does not necessarily mean that an organization will receive funding. Applicants should clearly demonstrate their track record, reach, measurable outcomes, and connection between the proposed funding and improved services for operating small and micro businesses. Is the Program Focused on Particular Industries? No. The program does not prioritize a specific industry or business sector. Instead, it is designed to strengthen Entrepreneurial Support Organizations that provide effective business-support services to small and micro businesses across the United States. When selecting organizations, the program will consider how the overall group of grantees represents different: Geographic areas Service models Communities served This approach means that applicants do not need to operate in one particular industry to be considered. How Does the Application Process Work? Applications must be submitted through the designated online application portal. Applicants will need to create an account and register their organization because the program is accepting applications from verified organizations. The application portal is administered through SurveyMonkey Apply. Importantly, applications cannot be submitted by email . Applicants can also review the application questions in advance through the program s application-question document. Required Financial Documents Applicants should prepare their financial documentation before submitting an application. The program requires: Audited financial statements for the organization s two most recently completed fiscal years; or Two years of IRS Form 990s if audited financial statements are not available. The organization s current board-approved operating budget showing anticipated revenues and expenses for 2026 and 2027. Having these documents ready can help organizations prepare their applications efficiently and ensure that required financial information is available before the deadline. How Many Applications Can an Organization Submit? Organizations may submit only one application per EIN/organization . Applicants should therefore make sure that their submission represents the organization s strongest and most complete application before final submission. When Will Applicants Receive a Decision? Applicants can expect to be notified of funding decisions by January 2027 . Successful grants will be one-time awards lasting 12 months , beginning in January 2027. What Happens After Organizations Receive Funding? Selected grantees will participate in the grant program for 12 months. Visa Foundation also plans to facilitate engagement opportunities throughout the grant period. These activities are intended to allow grantees to share: Lessons learned Challenges Best practices Experiences from implementing their programs This creates an opportunity for participating organizations to learn from one another while implementing their funded activities. Reporting Requirements Organizations receiving funding will be expected to submit a final narrative and financial report to Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors. The final reporting process will cover areas including: Progress made during the grant period Results achieved Lessons learned Key performance indicators Examples of indicators specifically identified by the program include: Number of small and micro businesses reached Number of jobs supported Revenue growth among supported businesses Applicants should therefore consider how they currently measure impact and how they will demonstrate results during the grant period. Important Application Deadline The deadline for submitting an application is: October 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM (noon) Pacific Time. Late applications will not be considered. Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications, particularly because the application requires organizational registration and supporting financial documentation. APPLY HERE Important Confidentiality and Application Terms Applicants should also pay attention to the terms governing application submissions. The program states that application submissions will not be treated as confidential . Applicants should therefore avoid including proprietary information, trade secrets, or other confidential information that they want to keep protected. Application information may be shared with Visa Foundation s program partners, including Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors and Maigent Partners, for program evaluation, administration, and reporting. The application information will be handled according to the Visa Privacy Policy and related application terms. By submitting an application, organizations also grant Visa Foundation a non-exclusive, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, reproduce, and distribute application materials for purposes related to program evaluation, administration, and reporting. The terms specify that this license does not transfer ownership of intellectual property to Visa Foundation. Who Makes the Final Grant Decisions? Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors is administering the program and the Request for Proposals process. As the legal grantor of record, RPA ultimately holds final authority over grantmaking decisions . CLICK HERE FOR MORE INFORMATION ON Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program Questions About the Program Applicants with programmatic questions can contact: EntrepreneurialSupportRFP@rockpa.org For grant-management questions, applicants can contact: grantsmanagement@rockpa.org Applicants are encouraged to review the available FAQs before contacting the program team. The organizers note that, because of the expected volume of inquiries, they may not be able to respond to every question before the application deadline. They also do not provide feedback on individual applications or proposals. Key Details at a Glance Detail Information Program Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program Opportunity Type Grant Total Funding Commitment $2 million Individual Grant Size $100,000–$250,000 Grant Duration 12 months Expected Start January 2027 Target Applicants Nonprofit Entrepreneurial Support Organizations Geographic Focus United States Eligible Areas 50 U.S. states, Washington, D.C., and U.S. territories Required Legal Status U.S.-based 501(c)(3) public charity Annual Budget Requirement $1 million–$10 million Financial History Two years of audited financial statements and/or IRS Form 990s Primary Beneficiaries Operating small and micro businesses Typical SMB Profile Generally 50 or fewer employees and $1.5 million or less in annual revenue Application Deadline October 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM PT Decision Timeline By January 2027 Applications by Email Not accepted Conclusion The Visa Foundation U.S. Small Business Growth and Innovation Program provides a significant funding opportunity for established nonprofit organizations working directly with small and micro businesses in the United States. With grants ranging from $100,000 to $250,000 , the program is intended to strengthen organizational capacity rather than simply finance individual business ideas. Eligible organizations can use the flexible funding to expand training, coaching, technical assistance, digital adoption initiatives, staffing, administrative capacity, and other activities that strengthen their ability to serve operating small and micro businesses. Organizations considering applying should carefully assess their eligibility, particularly their 501(c)(3) status, U.S. geographic focus, $1 million–$10 million annual operating budget, direct-service track record, financial documentation, and demonstrated impact on small and micro businesses . Applicants should also ensure that their proposed use of funds is clearly connected to improving business growth and resilience and that they can demonstrate measurable outcomes. The application deadline is October 21, 2026, at 12:00 PM Pacific Time , and late applications will not be accepted. Organizations interested in applying should begin preparing their financial documents, organizational information, impact evidence, and proposed use of funds well before the deadline. title: Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards 2027: $3,000 Scholarships and $4,000 Fellowships for Aspiring International Journalists
summary: Are you a university student seeking to build a career in international journalism , gain practical reporting experience, and develop your professional network with journalists around the world? The Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards 2027 provide financial support and professional opportunities for students interested in pursuing international journalism. The program typically awards 18 Scholar Awards each year. Depending on the award, recipients receive either a $3,000 scholarship for independent academic or journalistic work or a $4,000 fellowship that can support time working in the bureau of a leading news organization, including organizations such as the Associated Press, Reuters, and Bloomberg. The program is particularly focused on helping students launch careers in international journalism rather than supporting established mid-career professionals. Applicants can be of any nationality, provided they meet the program s stated eligibility requirements. The application deadline is Sunday, November 15, 2026 . About the Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards The Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards are designed to support emerging journalists who want to develop careers focused on international journalism. The program provides students with both financial assistance and opportunities to strengthen their journalism careers. In a typical year, the Foundation grants 18 awards , with recipients receiving either: A $3,000 scholarship to support independent work; or A $4,000 fellowship that can be used to fund time in the bureau of a leading news organization. Examples of organizations associated with fellowship placements include the Associated Press, Reuters, and Bloomberg . The program is primarily aimed at students who want to pursue international journalism as a career , making it particularly relevant for aspiring reporters, photojournalists, video journalists, and audio journalists interested in international issues and communities. Who Is the Overseas Press Club Foundation Looking For? The program is intended for students who are building their journalism careers and have demonstrated an interest in international journalism. The Foundation specifically states that applicants should be: College juniors; College seniors; or Graduate students; Enrolled in a degree program at the application deadline; and Demonstrably interested in international journalism. Applicants must also be currently enrolled full-time in a university program and satisfy one of the specified eligibility pathways: Be an international student studying at a U.S. college or university ; or Be a U.S. citizen studying abroad . The Foundation notes that its program is aimed at students of whatever nationality who want to pursue international journalism rather than simply return to their countries of origin to work as local reporters. What Funding Is Available? The Scholar Awards generally provide two forms of financial support. $3,000 Scholarship Some award recipients receive a $3,000 scholarship intended to support independent work and academic or journalistic goals. This can be particularly relevant for students who are developing independent journalism projects or pursuing academic goals connected to international journalism. $4,000 Fellowship Other recipients receive a $4,000 fellowship that can be used to fund time in a bureau of a leading news organization. The Foundation gives the Associated Press, Reuters, and Bloomberg as examples of major news organizations where such fellowship experiences may take place. The distinction means applicants should consider how their proposed work and career goals align with the type of support they hope to receive. What Does the Application Require? The application consists of three major components: A cover letter A resume A journalism work sample Applicants should prepare each component carefully because the Foundation provides specific instructions for each part of the submission. 1. Cover Letter The cover letter should be one page and autobiographical in nature. Applicants should use the letter to explain their development as a journalist and their reasons for pursuing international journalism. The Foundation suggests addressing questions such as: How did you develop an interest in journalism? Why are you interested in a particular part of the world? What international communities or issues interest you? How would you use the scholarship or fellowship to advance your journalism career? Are there any gaps or unusual leaps in your academic or professional progress that should be explained? The cover letter therefore provides an opportunity to connect the applicant s personal development, journalistic interests, international focus, and future career plans. 2. Resume Applicants must submit a one-page resume . The Foundation recommends emphasizing journalism-related experience and skills rather than providing an unnecessarily broad account of every activity. The resume should highlight: Previous journalism experience Language skills Media skills Visa or passport status relevant to working overseas International postings Domestic postings Published freelance work Independent unpublished journalism projects This information can help demonstrate both the applicant s journalism background and their ability to work in international settings. 3. Journalism Work Sample Applicants must select one type of work sample from the following categories: Print journalism Photojournalism Video journalism Audio journalism The requirements differ depending on the format selected. Print Journalism Work Sample Applicants choosing print journalism must submit a 600–800 word writing sample . The sample should focus on: An area of the world; or An international issue The topic should be consistent with the applicant s interests and experience. Applicants should also explain whether the work: Was previously published; Was edited or condensed; Was created as a school project. The Foundation provides examples of previous winning topics that have covered diverse international subjects, demonstrating that applicants do not necessarily need to report on conventional foreign-policy topics. Importantly, applicants do not need to have traveled abroad to apply . The Foundation notes that previous scholars have produced successful work about international communities and issues located within the United States, including reporting on Syrian and Lebanese immigrants in Brooklyn and Ukrainian refugees on Long Island. Important submission rule for writing samples Applicants should not send clips or URLs as their writing sample. Instead, the work should be reformatted into a standalone document . Applicants may include links to their other work on their resume. Photojournalism Work Sample Applicants choosing photojournalism should submit either: One PDF containing their photographs; or A link to a website where judges can view the work online. The entry can take the form of: A feature; A personality piece; or A news journalism project. The work may be narrated or may rely entirely on interviews and verité. Applicants must also provide a writing sample of approximately 500 words explaining the photographs. The written component should contextualize the images and explain: How the photographs were captured; and/or Why the photographs are significant. This means the application evaluates not only the images themselves but also the applicant s ability to explain the journalistic purpose and context of the work. Video and Audio Journalism Work Sample Applicants submitting video or audio work should provide a link where judges can view or listen to the submission. The work can be: A feature; A personality piece; or A news journalism piece. It can be narrated or rely primarily on interviews and verité. Length requirement The video or audio entry must be: At least 2 minutes long; and No longer than 7 minutes . The content should primarily have international interest . Applicants must also provide an approximately 500-word written explanation contextualizing the work. The explanation should address: How the images or audio were captured; Why the work is significant; What role the applicant played in producing it; and Appropriate credit for all team members who contributed. Each video or audio submission should demonstrate the full arc of the story , with a beginning, middle, and end. How to Submit the Application The Foundation requires applicants to combine all application elements into a single document . The accepted file formats are: .docx .pdf The document should be named using the following format: Last name_First name The file must not exceed 10 MB . Applicants can submit their application through the official submission page: Submit the Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Award Application Application Deadline The deadline for the Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards is: Sunday, November 15, 2026 Applicants should complete and submit all required materials before the deadline. What Makes a Strong Application? The Foundation provides several pieces of guidance about what judges respond well to. According to the application information, judges respond positively to applications demonstrating: Strong original reporting skills Color A clear sense of perspective A clear beginning, middle, and end Applicants are also advised to carefully proofread their materials. Applications that are exceedingly long may be disqualified , so candidates should follow the specified length requirements rather than adding unnecessary material. This makes it important for applicants to focus on the quality and clarity of their journalism rather than simply submitting a large quantity of work. International Business and Economic Journalism The Foundation has a specific area of interest in international business and economic coverage. Of the 18 awards, four are reserved for international business or economic coverage . The Foundation therefore encourages applicants interested in these areas to submit work demonstrating a strong understanding of global economic topics. Relevant topics mentioned by the Foundation include: Trade Finance Emerging markets Immigration Climate Public health Applicants interested in these areas can therefore consider submitting work that demonstrates their ability to report on global economic and interconnected international issues. AI Use and Originality Requirements The Foundation places an explicit requirement on the originality of application materials. All application material must be the result of the applicant s own journalism work. The Foundation also states that any use of AI must be: Responsible; and Clearly disclosed. Applicants should therefore make sure that their submitted journalism accurately represents their own reporting and that any AI use is disclosed according to the Foundation s requirement. Language Requirement All application materials must be submitted in English . If an applicant s original work was produced in another language, an English translation must be provided. This requirement applies to the application materials and should be taken into consideration when preparing a work sample originally produced in another language. Applicants Do Not Need International Travel Experience One potentially important point for aspiring international journalists is that applicants do not have to have traveled abroad to apply . The Foundation s examples demonstrate that international journalism can involve reporting on international communities and global issues within the United States. Previous scholars have reported on: Syrian and Lebanese immigrants in Brooklyn Ukrainian refugees on Long Island This means an applicant can demonstrate an international journalism perspective through reporting conducted domestically, provided the work engages meaningfully with international communities or issues. Scholar Awards Reception and Professional Development Award recipients will participate in a Scholar Awards reception in New York City in March 2027 . The event will form part of a two-day series of events involving: Relevant training Networking Professional journalists Winners are required to participate in the event. This provides recipients with an opportunity to connect with other journalists and professionals while participating in activities related to their development as international journalists. Join a Community of International Journalists The opportunity extends beyond the financial award. Recipients become part of a longstanding community of: International journalists Previous Scholar Award recipients Journalism professionals According to the Foundation, this network provides opportunities to: Build professional connections Exchange ideas Stay connected with other journalists throughout their careers For students beginning careers in international journalism, this community can form part of their longer-term professional network. Examples From Previous Scholar Award Recipients The Foundation highlights experiences from previous recipients to demonstrate how the awards have supported journalism careers. Youcef Bounab Youcef Bounab attended the Craig Newmark School of Journalism at CUNY. His award included a Harper s Magazine Scholarship and an OPC Foundation Fellowship with the Associated Press in Paris. According to his account, the fellowship gave him the opportunity to report from Paris and work on a wide range of stories, including interviews with government officials, the head of the Paris Olympic committee, booksellers, and others. He later became a Maghreb correspondent for Agence France-Presse, based in Tunisia and covering much of North Africa. Catherine Cartier Catherine Cartier attended New York University and received the Reuters Scholarship 2024 with an OPC Foundation Fellowship with Reuters in Dubai. Her fellowship involved reporting on: Finance Energy Breaking news She also interviewed people from different sectors and reported on developments in the Gulf region. According to her account, the experience influenced her subsequent international reporting. Brunella Tipismana Brunella Tipismana attended Yale University and received the Seymour and Audrey Topping Scholarship in 2024. The Foundation includes her among its previous Scholar Award recipients. Brett Simpson Brett Simpson attended the University of California-Berkeley Graduate School of Journalism and received the Irene Corbally Kuhn Scholarship in 2021. According to his account, the scholarship supported reporting in the Norwegian Arctic concerning an Indigenous rights protest related to a state-sanctioned copper mine on Sámi reindeer-herding lands. The resulting reporting appeared in National Geographic in 2022, and he described the experience as influential in shaping his subsequent reporting career focused on climate, energy, and human rights. Stephen Kalin Stephen Kalin attended the American University in Cairo and received the Roy Rowan Scholarship in 2013. He described using the scholarship to support a summer internship with Reuters, beginning in Lebanon and subsequently working on assignments in Egypt, Iraq, and Saudi Arabia. His account describes the early support as influential in his subsequent career in foreign reporting. How to Prepare a Competitive Application Although the Foundation provides specific requirements rather than a step-by-step preparation strategy, applicants can organize their preparation around the stated criteria. 1. Choose a clear international journalism focus Identify the international region, community, issue, or subject area that genuinely connects with your journalism interests. 2. Select your strongest work sample Choose one format: Print Photo Video Audio The selected work should demonstrate your journalism abilities and connect with your international interests. 3. Follow the format requirements exactly For example: Print: 600–800 words Photojournalism: photographs plus approximately 500 words of context Video/audio: 2–7 minutes plus approximately 500 words of context 4. Make your role clear For collaborative journalism, explain your specific contribution and properly credit other members of the team. 5. Keep your application focused The Foundation warns that exceedingly long applications may be disqualified. Follow the requested length requirements and avoid unnecessary material. 6. Proofread carefully The Foundation specifically advises applicants to carefully proofread their materials. 7. Address AI use appropriately If AI was used in preparing any application material, follow the Foundation s requirement that responsible AI use be clearly disclosed. Important Dates Date Event November 15, 2026 Application deadline Mid-January 2027 Winners expected to be contacted and posted on the Foundation s website March 2027 Scholar Awards reception and two-day training/networking event in New York City The Foundation states that winners will be contacted by mid-January and posted on its website. Frequently Asked Questions What is the Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Award? It is a student-focused journalism award program that provides financial support to students pursuing international journalism, with awards generally taking the form of scholarships or fellowships. How many awards are normally offered? In a typical year, the Foundation grants 18 Scholar Awards . How much funding can recipients receive? Recipients receive either a $3,000 scholarship or a $4,000 fellowship , depending on the award. Do I need to have traveled internationally? No. The Foundation explicitly states that applicants do not need to have traveled abroad to apply. Can my work focus on an international community in the United States? Yes. Previous examples cited by the Foundation include reporting on Syrian and Lebanese immigrants in Brooklyn and Ukrainian refugees on Long Island. Can graduate students apply? Yes. College juniors, college seniors, and graduate students enrolled in a degree program at the application deadline are identified as eligible applicant categories. What file formats are accepted? The complete application must be submitted as one document , using either .docx or .pdf , with a maximum size of 10 MB . What language must the application be in? Application materials must be submitted in English . Work originally produced in another language must be accompanied by an English translation. When is the deadline? The application deadline is Sunday, November 15, 2026 . Conclusion The Overseas Press Club Foundation Scholar Awards 2027 provide an opportunity for university students interested in international journalism to receive financial support while developing their journalism careers. The program typically offers 18 awards , with recipients receiving either a $3,000 scholarship or a $4,000 fellowship . The fellowship option can support time in the bureau of a major news organization, while the scholarship option can support independent work. Applicants can come from a variety of national backgrounds, but they must meet the program s specific enrollment requirements.
