title: ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship 2026/27 at the University of Leeds: Fully Funded PhD Opportunity
summary: The University of Leeds is offering a highly competitive ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship for postgraduate researchers interested in the changing relationship between digital technologies, artificial intelligence, skills, employment, regional economies and the future of work. The scholarship is based at Leeds University Business School and forms part of the ESRC Research Centre for Digital Futures at Work (Digit) , a major research centre focused on understanding how digital transformation is reshaping work, employment and society. For the 2026/27 academic cycle, the opportunity provides full academic fees together with a tax-free maintenance grant currently valued at £21,805 per year , with the maintenance amount increasing annually in line with UKRI rates. The funding is available for a period of up to 3.5 years for full-time study, making this a significant doctoral funding opportunity for applicants whose research interests align with the advertised project. The application deadline is 31 October 2026 , with the scholarship scheduled to begin on 1 February 2027 . There is one funding place available. About the ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship The scholarship is attached to a specific doctoral research project titled: “Building good work and digital skills within a regional digital eco-system.” The proposed research examines how local authorities and regional agencies can develop inclusive digital and skills ecosystems within regional labour markets. The project is particularly concerned with how regional economies respond to technological and economic restructuring and how institutions can support: Digital skills readiness Digital transformation within regional economies Adoption of artificial intelligence and digital technologies Digital skills upgrading Sustainable employment Good work Inclusive regional development Institutional capacity for supporting technological change The research will be situated within the United Kingdom’s broader strategy for digital adoption and economic growth. The studentship will use both qualitative and, where appropriate, quantitative research methods . It is expected to involve interviews with important actors such as local policymakers, employers and workers. The successful doctoral researcher will also collaborate with key local actors and undertake an internship connected to the research project. University of Leeds Research Environment The scholarship is located within the ESRC Research Centre for Digital Futures at Work (Digit) and based at Leeds University Business School. Digit is a multi-institutional research centre established in 2020 and led from the Universities of Leeds and Sussex. According to the University of Leeds, the centre has received £18 million in funding from the ESRC and provides a research environment for doctoral students and early-career researchers. Successful students will have access to Digit s doctoral and early-career researcher networks, alongside additional support for areas such as: Research consumables Training Conference attendance Doctoral and early-career research networks Research collaboration The wider research facilities of Leeds University Business School Leeds University Business School also houses a large academic department specialising in work and employment research through its People, Work and Employment Department . Scholarship Funding and Financial Support The ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship provides substantial financial support for doctoral study. For full-time study, the award includes: Full academic fees Maintenance grant of £21,805 for the 2026/27 session Annual increases to the maintenance grant in line with the UKRI rate Maintenance support for 3.5 years Full fee coverage for 3 years Part-time awards are provided on a pro-rata basis. This means the scholarship is designed to cover the principal university tuition costs while also providing a living-cost maintenance award during the doctoral programme. Important costs not covered International applicants should carefully consider additional costs associated with relocating to the United Kingdom. The University states that costs associated with international relocation are not covered by the scholarship . These may include: Visa expenses Insurance NHS fees Flights Other relocation-related expenses Applicants should therefore make separate financial arrangements for these costs. Research Focus: Digital Futures at Work The central research theme of the scholarship is the relationship between digital transformation, skills and employment . The doctoral project provides an opportunity to investigate how regional labour markets can adapt to rapid technological change while ensuring that workers and communities can benefit from emerging opportunities. Potential research questions within the broad project could relate to issues such as: How regional economies prepare for digital transformation. How governments and regional institutions can improve digital skills readiness. How artificial intelligence adoption affects regional labour markets. How workers can acquire new digital skills as industries change. How employers can support digital skills development. How regional institutions can promote sustainable employment. How technological change can be connected to the creation of good work. How policymakers can develop inclusive digital ecosystems. How local employers and workers experience digital transformation. How institutional capacity influences the adoption of emerging technologies. Applicants are not restricted to simply repeating the wording of the advertised project. The University states that applicants can pursue their own research interests within the broad area specified in the scholarship advertisement. Academic Entry Requirements Applicants are expected to meet the University of Leeds requirements for PhD candidates. Normally, applicants should have: A First Class or Upper Second Class British Bachelor s Honours degree, or an equivalent qualification from another country, in an appropriate discipline. A British Master s degree, an equivalent degree from an overseas university, or an equivalent professional qualification. For the People, Work and Employment area, a minimum average of 60% or equivalent in the Master s degree is required. Because this is a research-based doctoral opportunity, applicants should also demonstrate that their proposed research is academically appropriate and fits within the scope of the advertised research area. English Language Requirements Applicants whose first language is not English are required to provide evidence that they meet the University s minimum English language requirements. For research postgraduate study at Leeds University Business School, the stated requirement is: IELTS overall: 7.0 Minimum in each component: 6.5 An equivalent English language qualification may also be accepted. The test must be dated within two years of the course start date to remain valid. Applicants should therefore check the University s accepted alternatives if they intend to submit an English language qualification other than IELTS. Who Cannot Apply? There are important restrictions that applicants should understand before preparing an application. The scholarship is intended for new postgraduate researchers . Candidates who have already been awarded a PhD are excluded from applying. Applicants who are currently registered on a PhD are also excluded. However, the University indicates that applicants who previously studied for a PhD but did not complete it may be considered . The successful award must also be taken up by 1 February 2027 , and scholarship recipients are expected to live within a reasonable distance of the University of Leeds while receiving the scholarship. Application Process Applying for the scholarship requires applicants to first apply for a suitable research degree place at the University of Leeds. The University strongly recommends submitting the study application at least eight weeks before the scholarship deadline . This allows the Admissions team sufficient time to process the application and issue the required student identification number. Step 1: Apply for a PhD research place Applicants must first submit an application for a research degree through the University s online research degree application system. The scholarship cannot be considered independently of the relevant PhD study application. Step 2: Identify the scholarship Within the application, applicants should clearly state that they wish to be considered for: “The ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work centre scholarship.” Step 3: Identify the research area and supervisor Applicants should clearly state in the research section that their proposed research area is: Digital Futures at Work They should also identify the proposed supervisor as: Professor Mark Stuart Professor Mark Stuart and Professor Charles Umney are listed as the supervisors for the scholarship project. Step 4: Submit the required supporting documents Applicants must provide the documents required for their PhD study application. These include: Degree transcripts Degree certificates English language test results, where applicable Research proposal The research proposal is an especially important component of the application because it must demonstrate how the applicant s proposed research connects to the advertised research topic. APPLY HERE Research Proposal Requirements Applicants are expected to prepare a clear and academically rigorous research proposal. The proposal should remain within the broad subject specified in the scholarship advertisement while allowing the applicant to develop their own research interests within that area. The proposal should explain: What the applicant wants to research Why the proposed research is important How the research relates to the advertised topic The likely contribution of the research Relevant academic literature Recent policy debates relevant to the topic The proposed research methodology The planned approach to data collection The proposed approach to data analysis The University states that the PhD proposal should be no longer than six pages . A particularly important instruction is that proposals that are clearly written by AI will be desk rejected . Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposal genuinely represents their own research thinking, academic writing and intellectual contribution. Visit HERE for more guidance on writing a research proposal. Scholarship Deadline The official scholarship deadline is: 31 October 2026 The University states that applications must be complete by the stated deadline. It also specifies that study applications lacking the required documents by 17:00 on 31 October 2026 will not be considered for the award. Applicants should therefore avoid waiting until the final day to submit their materials, particularly because they must first apply for the PhD study place and obtain their student identification number. Click HERE for more information about ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship 2026/27 at the University of Leeds Funding Start Date The scholarship is scheduled to begin on: 1 February 2027 Successful candidates must be prepared to take up the award by this date. Selection Process Applications are considered after the deadline, and only complete applications will be considered. The University states that the final awards are based on academic merit . Financial hardship is not considered as a selection factor. Applicants should therefore concentrate on demonstrating: Strong academic preparation A clear and relevant research question Strong understanding of the research area A well-developed research methodology Knowledge of relevant literature Awareness of current policy debates A clear potential contribution to research Alignment with the advertised Digital Futures at Work project Ability to meet the requirements of doctoral-level study The University states that applicants will normally be emailed within six to eight weeks after the deadline to confirm the outcome of their application. A Research Opportunity at the Intersection of Technology, Skills and Employment The scholarship comes at an important intersection between digital transformation and the future of employment. As artificial intelligence, automation and digital technologies continue to influence workplaces and regional economies, questions surrounding digital skills, workforce adaptation, institutional readiness and sustainable employment are increasingly important areas of research. The advertised project provides a structured opportunity for a doctoral researcher to investigate these questions within a regional labour-market context. The inclusion of collaboration with local actors and an internship also means that the research is designed to engage with practical policy and workplace environments rather than being limited entirely to theoretical academic investigation. Supportive Research Environment Successful applicants will join a wider research environment through Digit and Leeds University Business School. The Digit centre provides doctoral and early-career researcher networks, while the Business School provides access to research facilities and an established academic community working on people, employment and work-related research. The scholarship also includes additional support for consumables, training and conference attendance, giving the successful researcher opportunities to develop academically and professionally during their doctoral studies. Diversity and Inclusion The University of Leeds states that it welcomes students from different backgrounds and countries and is committed to developing an inclusive academic community. The University particularly encourages applications from, among others, Black, Asian and minority ethnic communities, people who identify as LGBT+, and people with disabilities. However, the University states that applicants are selected on the basis of merit and ability . This means that there is no nationality or racial restriction attached to the scholarship, while applicants from diverse backgrounds are actively welcomed. Important Points Applicants Should Know Before submitting an application, prospective candidates should carefully consider the following: There is only one funding place. The scholarship is therefore highly competitive. You must first apply for the PhD research place. The scholarship application is connected to the University s research degree application process. Apply early. The University recommends submitting the study application at least eight weeks before the scholarship deadline. Your proposal must fit the research area. The proposed project should relate to Digital Futures at Work while allowing you to develop your own research interests within the specified scope. The proposal has a six-page limit. Applicants should keep the research proposal within this requirement. AI-generated research proposals are specifically prohibited. Proposals that are clearly written by AI may be rejected at the initial screening stage. International relocation expenses are not included. Applicants coming to the UK should budget separately for visas, insurance, NHS fees, flights and related costs. Existing PhD holders and current PhD students are excluded. Previous incomplete PhD study may be considered on a case-by-case basis. The scholarship must be taken up by 1 February 2027. Applicants must live within a reasonable distance of the University of Leeds while receiving the scholarship. Contact Information Applicants who require further information about the scholarship can contact the Leeds University Business School Admissions Team: Email: phd@lubs.leeds.ac.uk Applicants may also contact the listed supervisors: Professor Mark Stuart M.A.Stuart@lubs.leeds.ac.uk Professor Charles Umney C.R.Umney@leeds.ac.uk Key Details at a Glance Detail Information Scholarship ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship University University of Leeds Research centre ESRC Research Centre for Digital Futures at Work (Digit) School Leeds University Business School Research area Digital Futures at Work Project Building good work and digital skills within a regional digital eco-system Degree PhD Funding places 1 Funding Full academic fees + maintenance grant Maintenance £21,805 for 2026/27 Funding duration 3.5 years maintenance; 3 years full fees for full-time study Study mode Full-time or part-time Eligibility Home and international applicants Application deadline 31 October 2026 Funding start date 1 February 2027 Proposed supervisor Professor Mark Stuart English requirement IELTS 7.0 overall, minimum 6.5 in each component, or equivalent Research proposal Maximum six pages Previous/current PhD Generally excluded Relocation costs Not covered Conclusion The ESRC Centre for Digital Futures at Work Scholarship at the University of Leeds provides an opportunity for doctoral researchers to investigate how digital technologies, artificial intelligence, skills development and changing labour markets are shaping the future of work. The scholarship combines substantial financial support with access to a specialist research environment through the ESRC Research Centre for Digital Futures at Work and Leeds University Business School. The proposed research focuses specifically on building good work and digital skills within regional digital ecosystems, while allowing the successful researcher to develop their own research interests within the broader theme. With full academic fees, a £21,805 maintenance grant for 2026/27, research and training support, and funding for up to 3.5 years of full-time study , the opportunity is designed for strong doctoral candidates whose academic and research interests align with digital futures, skills, employment and regional economic transformation. Prospective applicants should begin the process early because they must first secure a research study application and prepare the required supporting documentation. The final scholarship deadline is 31 October 2026 , and the award is scheduled to commence on 1 February 2027 . title: Global Leadership Challenge 2026: Fully Funded Global Leadership Programme for Young Leaders
summary: The Global Leadership Challenge (GLC) 2026 is inviting applications from young leaders, postgraduate students and young professionals from around the world to join a global community focused on Responsible Leadership and addressing complex global challenges. The Global Leadership Challenge 2026 will bring together 100 young leaders selected through an open application process. Participants will engage with world-renowned academics, senior business and policy leaders, and other emerging leaders while developing action projects that address some of the most pressing challenges facing society. Applications are open from 29 September 2026 until 5 November 2026. The GLC 2026 will take place virtually from 10–14 December 2026 , allowing participants to join from around the world. Key Details — Global Leadership Challenge 2026 🌍 Programme: Global Leadership Challenge (GLC) 2026 👥 Participants: 100 young leaders 🎓 Who can apply: Students or young professionals 🌎 Eligibility: Applicants worldwide, all academic disciplines 💻 Format: Virtual 📅 GLC Dates: 10–14 December 2026 🗓️ Applications Open: 29 September 2026 ⏰ Deadline: 5 November 2026 🏆 Benefits: Certificate of Achievement, leadership training, mentorship, global networking and action projects ⭐ Additional opportunity: Top three teams may receive an all-expenses-covered invitation to the 56th St. Gallen Symposium in April 2027 📹 Application requirement: 40-second video in English Global Leadership Challenge 2026 The Global Leadership Challenge is designed for a diverse group of young people who are passionate about making a positive contribution to society and are ready to develop themselves as responsible leaders . GLC Members can participate virtually from anywhere in the world and will have the opportunity to collaborate across countries, disciplines and sectors. The programme focuses on developing leadership capabilities while encouraging participants to consider how leadership can contribute to the wider good of society . What You Will Gain from the Global Leadership Challenge Successful GLC participants will have the opportunity to: Become part of a diverse global community of young, responsible leaders . Engage with world-renowned academics and senior business and policy leaders . Develop action projects addressing some of the world s most pressing global challenges using design thinking principles . Learn to lead in a way that advances personal ambition while actively seeking the wider good of society . Earn an official Certificate of Achievement . Receive bespoke leadership training and mentorship offered by the Oxford Character Project . Potentially win an invitation to attend the 56th St Gallen Symposium in April 2027 , with all expenses covered , if your team is among the top three performing teams and is selected as Leaders of Tomorrow . Earn a Certificate of Achievement Participants who actively participate in all required GLC sessions can earn an official Certificate of Achievement . Attend the 56th St. Gallen Symposium Teams that perform among the top three may have the opportunity to attend the 56th St. Gallen Symposium in April 2027 as Leaders of Tomorrow , with all expenses covered. Receive Exclusive Mentorship After GLC GLC participants can also benefit from exclusive mentorship and leadership development opportunities following the programme. Who Can Apply for the Global Leadership Challenge 2026? The Global Leadership Challenge 2026 welcomes applications from people around the world and from all academic disciplines . To be eligible, applicants must meet the following criteria: Be a student currently enrolled in a Master s or PhD programme , or a young professional aged between 21 and 30 years . Have completed their undergraduate studies . Have demonstrated a commitment to Responsible Leadership through extracurricular activities and/or work experience. Be available to invest approximately five half-days from 10–14 December 2026 in the GLC. Be able to actively participate in all GLC sessions. Active participation in all GLC sessions is mandatory to receive a Certificate of Achievement. The organisers are seeking a diverse group of postgraduate students and young professionals who are ready to engage with complex global challenges and develop their leadership capabilities. Global Leadership Challenge 2026 Application Deadline Applications for the GLC 2026 are being accepted according to the following timeline: Important Date Details 29 September 2026 Application Opens 5 November 2026 Application Closes 10–14 December 2026 Global Leadership Challenge 2026 Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so applicants are encouraged to apply early rather than waiting until the deadline. Global Leadership Challenge 2026 Challenge Information As part of the programme, participants will work on challenges connected to major global issues and engage with challenge partners. Swiss Re Challenge Working with Swiss Re , participants will explore how organisations can build a future-ready workforce in a world where technology, risk and expectations are changing rapidly. The challenge will examine how human expertise, critical thinking and artificial intelligence (AI) can come together to rethink work, strengthen judgement and build the capabilities required for the future. Schwarzman Scholars Challenge The Schwarzman Scholars Program is also involved in the Global Leadership Challenge. Participants will explore how leadership education and curriculum can evolve to equip the next generation of global leaders with the tools needed to navigate uncertainty. Additional Challenge Partner The organisers are finalising another challenge partner, with further details expected to be announced. What You Need Before Applying Applicants should prepare the following information and documents before starting their Global Leadership Challenge 2026 application . 1. Personal Information Applicants should be ready to provide personal information, including: Full address Email address Other contact details 2. Required Documents Applicants should prepare: CV in PDF format Recent portrait picture in JPEG or PNG format Proof of enrolment in PDF format for students 3. Application Questions Applicants will also be asked to respond to several questions and complete a short video task. Keynote Choice Suggest a keynote speaker who could inspire global leaders to act responsibly. Your Message Record a maximum 40-second video in English inspiring global leaders to practice Responsible Leadership . Your Action Share one concrete example in no more than 50 words explaining how you personally put Responsible Leadership into practice. Ensure the settings allow anyone with the link to view the video. Make sure viewers do not require a login, password or organisation account. Paste the video link into the designated field in the Global Leadership Challenge application form . Why Apply for the Global Leadership Challenge 2026? The GLC provides an opportunity for young leaders and postgraduate students to connect with an international community, engage with senior leaders and academics, develop practical action projects and strengthen their understanding of Responsible Leadership . The programme also provides opportunities for leadership training, mentorship, collaboration and recognition through a Certificate of Achievement .
